• Data shows organizations are deploying AI in workflows beyond pilots, with 64% seeing returns on AI investments, up 10 points from 2025
  • As AI moves deeper into the business, leaders also report their average readiness for external risks fell to 24% — down 7 points from 2025 — a decline evident across industries and countries
  • 71% of leaders say their IT estate is mostly or fully modernized, yet 66% of CIOs believe their infrastructure requires significant re-architecture before it can support AI at scale

, /PRNewswire/ -- Kyndryl (NYSE: KD), a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services, today released the findings from its third annual Readiness Report, revealing a widening divide between the returns organizations are seeing from AI and their readiness to manage the risks and demands that come with it.

While 64% of leaders report positive returns on AI investments, up 10 points from 2025, average readiness across external risks fell seven points to 24%. The steepest declines were in readiness for cyber threats and competitive disruption, as AI puts new pressure on business models, technology foundations and how organizations operate.

This year's report captures the attitudes and actions of 3,700 senior business leaders across 21 countries. The data shows a dichotomy: while organizations are racing to deliver returns on significant AI investments, they simultaneously feel ill-equipped to navigate the implications for the AI era.

"As AI creates significant opportunity, organizations are now focusing on how to make early returns sustainable," said Martin Schroeter, Chairman and CEO, Kyndryl. "This year's Readiness Report shows a new kind of readiness gap: AI ambitions are moving faster than the systems needed to support them, and the bar for readiness keeps moving as AI becomes more integrated in enterprises. Our data shows that focusing on people, technology and governance can help organizations win with AI and keep the ability to adapt as opportunities evolve."

The report shows how organizations are making progress and adapting their AI strategies:

  • Significantly fewer describe themselves as in the experimentation phase compared to a year ago (-13 points from 2025, to 49%)
  • Nearly half (48%) substantially changed their AI strategies this year, with implications across tech, people and governance
  • About a quarter (24%) saw an AI investment fail, and 21% canceled a major AI initiative

The transition from experimentation to broader, sustained adoption remains uneven, particularly in the workforce and talent. Organizations have further to go in adapting how people work:

  • Just 27% have formally updated roles and responsibilities around AI
  • 29% have fully implemented change management for AI adoption at their organizations
  • Those who have done both are 28 points more likely to be completely ready for their AI implementation, and are 8 points more likely to report positive ROI on their AI investments

Additional findings in the report include:

Security concerns drive down confidence
For the third year in a row, security concerns topped the list of external risks, and this year contributed most to the overall decline in readiness. Just 26% of firms said they were completely ready for cyberattacks, a drop of 11 points from last year. Three in four leaders say AI helps their organizations identify threats faster, even as confidence in their ability to respond to cyberattacks has declined.

Concern about AI challenges established business models
The second-largest drop in readiness came from leaders' concerns about competitive disruptions outside of their industry (-10 points from 2025, to 23%). The finding comes as AI agents and other new technologies are being deployed to erode established industry boundaries, and leaders described both challenges of adopting new technologies and questioning established products and business models.

Retailers, for instance, are weighing how to benefit from AI shopping assistants without forfeiting direct customer relationships; software companies face questions about SaaS models as AI rebalances the build-versus-buy equation; and financial institutions are challenged by emerging lending models.

Leaders put a premium on sovereignty, but action remains limited
The research also captures how leaders are considering digital sovereignty in a year marked by greater actions by governments, most visibly in the European Union. Notably, leaders in the EU are slightly less likely to have taken sovereignty-related actions compared to those in the rest of the world. It also captures the trade-offs organizations may need to make: 68% say solutions offering full operational control, should they need it, are worth a premium of 10% or more, and 60% say greater control is worth slower deployment and adoption of advanced capabilities.

Modernized infrastructure isn't necessarily AI-ready
For the third year in a row, leaders said upgrading their IT infrastructure was the number one action their organizations are taking to mitigate external risks, and 71% rate their infrastructure as mostly or fully modernized. Yet two-thirds of CIOs surveyed think their technology foundations need significant re-architecture before being fully ready for AI at scale. Leaders are also making a distinction between a modern IT estate and one ready for the increased demands of artificial intelligence.

Read the Kyndryl Readiness Report.

• 数据显示，各组织正将AI部署到试点之外的工作流程中，64%的组织已从AI投资中获得回报，较2025年上升10个百分点
  • 随着AI更深入地融入业务，领导者也表示，他们应对外部风险的平均准备就绪率降至24%，较2025年下降7个百分点，各行业和各国均出现这一下降趋势
  • 71%的领导者表示，其IT环境已大部分或完全实现现代化，但66%的首席信息官认为，其基础设施需要进行重大架构重构，才能支持大规模应用AI

, /PRNewswire/ -- 关键任务型企业技术服务的领先提供商Kyndryl （纽约证券交易所代码：KD）今日发布了第三份年度《准备就绪报告》的调查结果，揭示出各组织从AI中获得的回报，与其管理随之而来的风险和需求的准备程度之间，差距正在扩大。

64%的领导者表示，AI投资带来了正向回报，较2025年上升10个百分点；但应对各类外部风险的平均准备就绪率下降了7个百分点，降至24%。应对网络威胁和竞争性冲击的准备程度降幅最大，AI正对商业模式、技术基础和组织运营方式施加新的压力。

今年的报告记录了21个国家的3,700名企业高管的态度与行动。数据显示出一种矛盾：各组织正竞相推动大规模AI投资产生回报，同时却觉得自己尚未做好充分准备，以应对AI时代带来的影响。

Kyndryl董事长兼首席执行官Martin Schroeter表示：“AI正在创造重大机遇，各组织如今正着力于如何让早期回报持续下去。今年的《准备就绪报告》揭示了一种新的准备差距：AI雄心的发展速度超过了支撑这些雄心所需系统的建设速度，而随着AI进一步融入企业，准备就绪的标准也在不断变化。我们的数据显示，聚焦人员、技术和治理，可以帮助各组织借助AI取得成功，并在机遇不断演变时保持适应能力。”

报告展示了各组织如何取得进展并调整其AI战略：

  • 与一年前相比，自认为仍处于试验阶段的组织明显减少（较2025年下降13个百分点，降至49%）
  • 近一半（48%）的组织今年大幅调整了AI战略，影响涉及技术、人员和治理各方面
  • 约四分之一（24%）的组织曾有一项AI投资失败，21%的组织取消了一项重大AI计划

从试验转向更广泛、持续的应用，这一转变的进展仍不均衡，尤其体现在员工队伍和人才方面。各组织在调整人员工作方式方面仍有更多工作要做：

  • 仅27%的组织已正式更新与AI相关的岗位和职责
  • 29%的组织已在内部全面实施针对AI应用的变革管理
  • 两项都已完成的组织，其完全做好AI实施准备的比例高出28个百分点，报告AI投资获得正向投资回报的比例高出8个百分点

报告的其他发现包括：

安全担忧削弱信心
安全担忧连续第三年位居外部风险榜首，今年也是整体准备程度下降的最大影响因素。仅26%的企业表示已为网络攻击做好充分准备，较去年下降11个百分点。四分之三的领导者表示，AI帮助其组织更快地识别威胁，但他们对自身应对网络攻击能力的信心却有所下降。

AI冲击既有商业模式引发担忧
准备程度降幅第二大的领域，是领导者对来自本行业之外的竞争性冲击的担忧（较2025年下降10个百分点，降至23%）。这一发现的背景是，AI智能体和其他新技术正在被部署应用，逐步打破既有行业边界。领导者既谈到了采用新技术所面临的挑战，也对既有产品和商业模式提出了质疑。

例如，零售商正权衡如何在不失去与客户直接联系的情况下，从AI购物助手中受益；随着AI重新改变自主开发与购买之间的权衡，软件公司的SaaS模式面临质疑；金融机构则受到新兴借贷模式的挑战。

领导者高度重视主权，但行动仍然有限
在各国政府加大行动力度、尤其是欧盟行动最为明显的一年里，这项研究也记录了领导者如何看待数字主权。值得关注的是，与世界其他地区的领导者相比，欧盟领导者采取主权相关行动的比例略低。研究还记录了各组织可能需要作出的权衡：68%的受访者表示，对于能在需要时提供全面运营控制权的解决方案，支付10%或更高的溢价是值得的；60%的受访者表示，为了获得更大的控制权，可以接受先进能力的部署和采用速度放缓。

基础设施实现现代化，并不一定意味着已为AI做好准备
领导者连续第三年表示，升级IT基础设施是其组织为缓解外部风险而采取的首要行动，71%的领导者认为其基础设施已大部分或完全实现现代化。然而，三分之二的受访首席信息官认为，其技术基础需要进行重大架构重构，才能为大规模应用AI做好充分准备。领导者也开始区分现代化的IT环境与能够满足人工智能不断增长需求的IT环境。

阅读《Kyndryl准备就绪报告》。
